description: Driven by innovation, united by purpose. Building impactful solutions and turning bold ideas into lasting success.
summary:
SKYFORGE Fire Atlas is an interactive research dashboard that helps users explore NASA’s microgravity combustion findings. It combines an AI assistant with a searchable Library, original PDF viewing, trial comparisons, and dedicated analysis tools. Users can ask questions in English or Uzbek, inspect supporting evidence, and verify answers against source documents.

Our project addresses the Flame in Freefall challenge by making complex research easier to find, compare, and understand. It distinguishes observed results from assumptions and synthetic calculations, and reports when supporting evidence is unavailable. By connecting AI assistance with independent source inspection, Fire Atlas aims to support research, education, and informed discussion of fire safety for future space exploration.
details:
SKYFORGE Fire Atlas connects conversational research assistance with direct access to NASA sources. Users can browse studies independently or ask the AI assistant a question. For research questions, the system retrieves relevant indexed passages and produces answers with source references, including available page, table, and trial identifiers. Users can then open the original documents in the Library to check the evidence themselves.

The current demonstration includes five NASA PSI studies, 370 verified downloaded files, and 61 PDFs. Downloaded files and AI-searchable content are tracked separately: the complete downloaded collection has not yet been indexed. Dedicated tools support evidence ranking, statistical estimation, and conditional scenarios. Physical ranking currently uses three source-checked BASS-II trials. Synthetic calculations are explicitly labeled, while scenarios separate observations, assumptions, and proposed follow-up experiments.

The application uses React, Vite, JavaScript, Node.js, Python, SQLite, PDF.js, and multilingual E5 embeddings through Transformers.js. AI responses use OpenRouter. The frontend is hosted on Netlify, with data and backend services running on a Windows server connected through HTTPS. AI coding tools also assisted development.

Our creative approach gives users two complementary ways to investigate: AI-assisted discovery and independent source verification. We prioritized scientific traceability, preservation of original units, clear uncertainty, English–Uzbek accessibility, and usability on both phones and desktops. The intended impact is to help researchers and learners navigate combustion evidence more efficiently without presenting unsupported predictions as established scientific findings.
